title: Majority Element II
summary: Given an integer array of size n, identify all elements that occur more than n / 3 times.
statement: Given an integer array of size n, identify all elements that occur more than n / 3 times.
constraints: Return every value occurring STRICTLY more than floor(n/3) times, in any order. There can be zero, one, or two such values.
hints: At most two values can each occur more than one third of the time.
Maintain two Boyer–Moore candidates and cancel groups of three different values.
First select candidates in one pass; then count both candidates in the original list and retain only strict majorities.
Candidate selection alone is not proof. The final verification pass handles arrays with no qualifying value.
editorial: Canceling one occurrence from each of three distinct values cannot remove a true over-one-third majority from candidacy. Two counters therefore suffice, but the survivors must be verified because cancellation can leave nonmajorities. The independent oracle directly counts every distinct value.

tests.explanation: With n=3, a value must occur more than once; 3 occurs twice.
floor(2/3)=0, so both one-occurrence values qualify and both must be returned.
